source.title: Safe Evolution with Circuit Anchors
source.authors: Yan Liu; Jie Fu; Tsung-Yi Ho

page_placements.theme: Safety processing depends on layers, heads and feature circuits

record.tranche_reason: The study identifies sparse transcoder-feature circuits and intervenes on their activations to test whether they causally affect refusal. This is a conceptual test of safety localization, not a test of weight or rank localization.
record.gate_note: The study tests feature-circuit localization and safety under self-evolution. It does not test harmful or benign fine-tuning, token-position KL concentration, compliant prefills, suffixes, decoding changes, or spreading safety beyond the first response tokens. Results cited about fine-tuning are not study results.
record.test_reason: The study's own experiments show that benign capability training lowers refusal on held-out AdvBench harmful prompts in three instruction-tuned models. The training is self-evolution RL on math or self-proposed reasoning tasks (EVOL-RL, Abs-ZERO), with no harmful data. This is a new training setting for V2. Its circuit-localization results are feature-level, not weight or rank-level, so they do not test V5 as stated.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. Add that the authors find circuit anchoring (CAE) beats an explicit reward-model safety constraint on both safety and capability, at lower cost. Add that they call safety degradation an inherent risk of unconstrained self-evolution.
record.recipe_differences: The study examines self-evolution of instruction-tuned models and circuit-activation interventions, rather than fine-tuning on a few harmful or benign examples or testing token-position KL and compliant openings.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary with evolution algorithm, model family, evolution horizon, and CAE constraint weight. Activation scaling of the identified circuit changes refusal, while scaling a same-size random circuit does not systematically do so.

fits_no_version.finding: A transcoder-feature circuit making up 1.2%–1.8% of features causally mediates refusal. Zeroing it drops Llama refusal 96.2%→48.7%; a random same-size set shows no trend (±8%).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal is mediated by a sparse set of transcoder features whose ablation roughly halves refusal on held-out harmful prompts.

fits_no_version.finding: Anchoring safety-circuit feature activations during self-evolution keeps safety above 95%, with near-equal capability gains, including on a 9B model and over 5,000 steps.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Activation-level anchoring of a safety feature circuit prevents safety erosion during benign RL training.

record.problems: Numerical refusal results for the causal intervention are reported in prose for a model name that conflicts with the Figure 3 panel label. Many per-model and per-condition results are shown only in figures or described in aggregate; no uncertainty estimates are stated. The localization result is a share of transcoder features, not weights or ranks.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 2 and Figure 5 contain separate plotted trajectories whose exact values are not stated in the text; they are represented only by the aggregate Figure 2 description and aggregate CAE result where available. Figure 4's constraint-weight curves are not extracted because the claim versions do not concern the self-evolution constraint-weight trade-off.

untested.parts: No supervised fine-tuning on benign instruction data. No carefully selected benign data. No models above 9B. Only RL self-evolution on reasoning tasks.
No per-token KL between aligned and base models.
No prefilling, suffix or decoding attacks.
Localization is measured over transcoder features, not weights or ranks. No parameter-pruning or rank test.
No test of data or objective as the cause of shallowness.
CAE anchors feature activations; it does not train safety beyond the early response tokens or measure token depth.

missing.what: Per-model refusal drops annotated on Figure 2: EVOL-RL 23.6%, 24.5%, 29.2%; Abs-ZERO 26.1%, 27.4%, 25.9%. These are the only per-model Abs-ZERO numbers.
Results for the reward-model (Beaver-Cost) constraint, which only partly arrests the safety decline. These are mitigation results, not needed for the verdict.

record.verdict_notes: The record's V5 'supports' label is dropped. The feature-level localization is a related but different construct from V5's weights or ranks, so it is recorded under fits_no_version. The record's 'none' links for the unconstrained-evolution rows are changed to V2, since benign reasoning RL raising harmful compliance is V2's effect in a new setting. Several inconsistencies in the paper: the model name (Llama-3.2-2B vs 1B), λ (0.1 vs 0.8), and the 9B unconstrained safety score duplicating Qwen's 69.85%. The paper reports no uncertainty estimates.

versions.untested_parts: No fine-tuning on harmful examples or test of harmful-request compliance after such fine-tuning.
No ordinary or carefully selected benign fine-tuning data.
No per-token KL comparison between aligned and base models.
No compliant opening, suffix, or decoding intervention.
The study measures and intervenes on transcoder features, not weights or ranks; it does not establish what share of model parameters carries safety.
No test of whether data or a training objective causes first-token shallowness.
CAE anchors circuit activations during self-evolution, but the study does not train or measure safety distributed beyond early response tokens.
